topic: Idempotent webhook handlers: why duplicate events happen and how to handle them
text:
Your webhook handler will receive the same event twice. Probably this week.

Most providers deliver webhooks "at least once", Stripe and GitHub included. A timeout on your side, a slow deploy, a network blip, and they retry. If your handler isn't ready for that, one payment turns into two orders, two emails, two invoices.

The fix is boring, and it works: make the handler idempotent.

1. Record the event ID before doing any work. A unique index on event_id is enough.
2. If that ID already exists, return 200 and stop. The provider only needs to know you received it.
3. Push the slow work (emails, fulfilment, third-party calls) to a background job and respond fast. Slow handlers are the main reason retries happen in the first place.
4. Make the job itself safe to run twice: "set status = paid", not "add 1 to balance".

In Postgres, step 1 and 2 are a single query:

INSERT INTO processed_events (event_id) VALUES ($1)
ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING
RETURNING event_id;

No row back means you've already handled it.

Retries aren't the bug. Assuming they won't happen is.

Have you ever been bitten by a duplicate webhook or a retry in production? What did it break, and how did you fix it?

image.alt: Animated blueprint-style flow: a webhook provider sends an event to POST /webhooks, the handler checks whether the event ID was already seen; a new event is saved and queued for a worker, a duplicate retry returns 200 and stops. Signed Ali Hassan, alihexan.com.
